doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Joe Williams and Hinton recall a Club DeLisa singer and Alberta Hunter
summary: Williams tells a bawdy story about a singer at the Club DeLisa; they try to recall the name of the woman at The Cookery and land on Alberta Hunter, who emceed at the Indiana Theater.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. I keep my eye on the ladies, you know. My first one she was a real lady. She was a doll. And as I say this woman, it was either her or the one with the one eye. What was the one that had the one eye? What was her name, Hop? Anyhow, so she walked over the stage, you know, went down, the show was over, the Club DeLisa you know, so here comes the strolling singer and this woman. And she walked up to him and she started right away. [sings] I’m going to lock my car and throw away the key, I’m tired of you sticking those great big dicks in me. My wife went [gasps] like she said there was nowhere to run.
John Vanmore used to come around to see her all the time.
Yeah. Chippy. Chippy. Yeah, Chippy, Chippy.
Yeah, I know those names, that made all them records, [inaudible] show biz and made a big success.
What was that lady’s name, that worked at The Cookery?
But you remember Mr. Simmons? The lady that used to work at The Cookery? Made such a big — © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
Roberta what? NS: Was it Roberta or Rosetta?
No. Jillean? We’re trying to think of the lady’s name who made such a big hit, came back at the Cookery who hadn’t been out in a long time?

That’s right. She used to be the emcee at the Indiana Theater, and we were all young, and they’d say, “We’re going to give you Alberta Hunter.” We’d say “booooo.” NS: She was, we’re talking about good improvisation, because she could get one note, and sing that whole line and hold that one note.
All on that one note, you got it.
